body.estimand_functional: \(\mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)=\{A_{vu}z/(1-A_{vv}z):(A,D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\}\), with \(\operatorname{Cert}_{uv,m,G}(B,Q)\) returning its unique element or two attained unequal elements

sampling_model.design: A single stationary Gaussian fine-grid VAR(1) is observed systematically at times \(0,m,\ldots,nm\), with known \(m\) and supplied labeled process DAG \(G\).
sampling_model.units: The sampling units are the \(n+1\) dependent coarse-time vectors \((Y_0,\ldots,Y_n)\).
sampling_model.treatment: There is no binary treatment; the causal intervention is a unit perturbation transmitted along the direct process edge \(u\to v\).
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; stability keeps \(1-A_{vv}z\ne0\) on \(\mathbb T\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \((M_0,M_1)\) by overlapping empirical lag moments. On the derivative-separated odd stratum, map them through \((\widehat B,\widehat Q)\), the graph recursion, and the rational transfer, and use the Isserlis long-run covariance with the recursive Jacobian for simultaneous Wald disks. Globally, invert the rationally outward-rounded moment box through all fine-grid branches; the constant covariance-envelope fallback is measurable and coincides pathwise with that deterministic box.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under the Gaussianity assumption of the data, the solutions are generally not unique.
We present a unifying framework for parameter identifiability and estimation under both subsampling and mixed frequencies when the shocks are non-Gaussian.
The algorithm forms a Schur decomposition and computes a \(p\)-th root of the triangular factor by a recursion.
The spectral latent-factor half-trek criterion identifies direct link functions by rational operations on the spectral density.
We characterise the asymptotic distribution of causal effect and spectral contribution estimators in terms of algebraic relations dictated by the process graph.
We establish useful deviation bounds for dependent Gaussian data using a spectral measure of stability.
We prove an exponential probability tail inequality for positive semidefinite quadratic forms in a subgaussian random vector.
The results about coverage probability are stated in a nonasymptotic way and apply for small and moderate sample size.
We provide a constraint satisfaction procedure for system-timescale causal structures corresponding to a measurement-timescale structure.
Classical CAD projection algorithms preserve chordal structure when projection follows a perfect elimination ordering.
In the regular mixed-frequency VARMA case with moving-average order exceeding autoregressive order, generic local identification fails.

body.tldr: Subsampling turns a fine-grid process DAG into a matrix-root problem, so causal identification depends on the complete root-and-innovation fiber rather than on a selected numerical root. The paper gives parity-sharp graph recursion and exact transfer-aware algebraic certification. On the explicitly defined derivative-separated odd stratum, a uniformly valid delta method yields simultaneous Wald disks; the stratum is nonempty exactly in the feasible separation range. Globally, a finite-sample coarse-moment region is inverted through every branch, and the measurable constant-envelope fallback reproduces the deterministic moment box pathwise, preserving coverage without claiming a strict adaptive gain.

project_justification.gap: Published subsampling results either invoke non-Gaussian shocks to identify the fine model, enumerate qualitative graph equivalence classes, or choose a numerical matrix-root branch. Published process-graph effect theory begins with fine-grid spectral information, and its Wald theory is local. No result decides a queried Gaussian transfer over the complete graph- and covariance-compatible root fiber.
project_justification.niche: A supplied causal order makes triangular root recursion available, while diagonal fine innovations make the coarse covariance an informative branch filter. Divided-difference zero sets isolate a small but essential singular problem that exact real algebraic methods can decide without pretending the parameter fiber is closed or finite.
project_justification.fill: The project gives a parity-sharp graph recursion, a universal even-factor same-law obstruction, a total transfer-aware CAD fallback with exact witnesses, simultaneous Wald disks on an explicit derivative-separated odd class, and finite-sample branch-free inversion of a rationally rounded coarse-moment region. The covariance-envelope fallback is measurable and pathwise no wider because it exactly reproduces the deterministic box; it is a validity fallback, not an adaptive improvement.

body.related_work: Gong et al. (2015) motivate causal-frequency recovery and prove non-Gaussian identification, while their Gaussian discussion supplies the broad nonuniqueness against which the parity certificate is positioned. Tank, Fox, and Shojaie (2019) also use non-Gaussian shocks and likelihood methods, so their information regime is complementary rather than a Gaussian comparator. Hyttinen et al. (2017) preserve qualitative subsampling ambiguity through exact constraints; the present target is a numerical rational transfer. Smith (2003), Bini, Higham, and Meini (2005), and Higham (2008) supply the triangular-root recursion and branch theory; the new content begins when graph zeros, the diagonal-innovation covariance equation, transfer equality, and complete fiber certification are imposed jointly. Reiter et al. (2026) identify rational link effects from the unaliased fine-grid spectrum, and Reiter et al. (2024) derive local delta-method inference once fine-grid coefficients are differentiably estimable. Basu and Michailidis (2015), Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang (2012), and Giurcanu and Spokoiny (2004) provide the concentration ingredients for a finite-sample lag-moment region. Li et al. (2023) and Wilson et al. (2014) inform the exact algebraic fallback but do not analyze this compatibility system. Deistler, Koelbl, and Anderson (2017), Anderson et al. (2016), and Gersing, Sögner, and Deistler (2023) show that mixed-frequency retrieval changes sharply across VAR, VARMA, and unit-root classes; those extensions are outside the present stationary VAR(1) scope.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The genericity claim is made in fine-parameter space, not in the image space of observed coarse laws. Exact CAD has worst-case doubly exponential complexity, and the proposal certifies termination rather than polynomial-time scalability. For arbitrary unnamed real inputs, Tarski--Seidenberg gives relative definability only; executable witness extraction requires an effective real closed field or verified rational input intervals. The Temperature--Ozone example in Gong et al. is used only as a conditional \(m=2\) Gaussian ambiguity audit if an external scientific argument supplies the one-way order; their fitted model does not establish that order.
body.honest_scope: The algebraic identification and ambiguity results concern stable, ordered, finite-dimensional Gaussian VAR(1) systems with known subsampling factor, supplied labeled process DAG, and diagonal fine-grid innovation covariance. Under the supplied order and queried-edge conditions, the Wald theorem is local to the odd-factor class with both divided-difference and diagonal-root derivative separation; this class is nonempty exactly when \(\kappa\le m(1-\gamma)^{m-1}\). The limiting covariance may be singular across frequencies but is uniformly nonzero in the queried-edge direction. Outside that class, inference uses branch-free inversion rather than branch selection. The constant covariance-envelope construction proves finite-sample validity and equality of widths with the deterministic box, not strict adaptive improvement. Exact CAD certifies termination rather than polynomial-time scalability, and executable witnesses require effective real-closed-field input. No claim is made about unknown causal order, unknown sampling factor, high-dimensional rates, VARMA or unit-root extensions, or the scientific validity of the Temperature--Ozone ordering.
